model.name: Fbn2 ΔRAD21 baseline candidate · 20 Mb at 10 kb

warnings: No physical unit mapping is attached; model values remain in reduced units.
Dynamics are stored in reduced units. Physical interpretation requires a documented length scale and an MSD-derived clock; attaching a mapping does not validate the biological model.
Speckles and nucleoli are imposed stationary affinity fields. Protein assemblies can form independently; nucleolar subphases and rRNA processing are not modeled.
IDRs are explicit domain-bead sticker chains, not residue-level or sequence-parametrized CALVADOS proteins.
Independent particle drag omits hydrodynamic coupling; soft excluded volume can allow chain crossings.
Histone marks are independent binary flags per bead; a nucleosome-unit bead can carry these flags but does not resolve histone tails, individual residues, or wrapped DNA.
Regulatory gains and state-selective chromatin attraction are configurable hypotheses; protein preferences are encounter multipliers, not measured dissociation constants.
Transcription-dependent persistence and processing enhancement are configurable hypotheses, not universal biological laws.
Assembly and gene parameters are illustrative. Seeing a cluster is not evidence of calibrated liquid-liquid phase separation.
No physical length/time mapping is attached. Times and diffusion coefficients cannot yet be read as biological seconds or micrometers squared per second.

Coarse genomic resolution: each bead represents 10,000 bp. Individual nucleosomes, promoters, and other sub-bead features are unresolved. Changing bp per bead does not calibrate or rescale diffusion, mechanics, or reaction rates.
Each replica starts from the model and its own seed; this export does not resume the current viewer state.
Forces, reactions and RNA diffusion run on CPU. CUDA or OpenCL runs only the Brownian integrator on the selected device; acceleration is not guaranteed. OpenCL device type may be CPU or GPU.
Memory, walltime and GPU availability are scheduler requests, not capacity estimates. Pilot the model before a large array.
Existing model particle and transcript limits still apply. A GPU request does not enable a 100,000-nucleosome model.
SLURM GPU and queue directives are site-specific; inspect the template before submitting.
One GPU is requested per independent replica. Default device selection uses the devices visible on the allocated node; requested GPU failures stop the run.

Large output request: 16,004 full snapshots and 1,604 metric records across all replicas. JSON snapshots include positions, tracks, proteins and RNA; check disk capacity and consider wider sampling intervals.

scripts.slurm:
#!/bin/sh
#SBATCH --job-name=fbn2-baseline
#SBATCH --array=0-3
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --ntasks=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --time=3-00:00:00
#SBATCH --output=slurm-%A_%a.out
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
set -eu
# Submit from the extracted bundle directory. Adapt GPU/queue directives to your site.
cd -- "${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR:?Submit this script from the extracted bundle directory}"
# Do not replace CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: the scheduler owns GPU visibility.
sh ./run.sh "${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID:?Missing array task ID}"
scripts.shell:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
# Run from the extracted bundle; activate a prepared Python environment first.
cd -- "$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)"
REPLICA=${1:-0}
case "$REPLICA" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "Replica must be a nonnegative integer." >&2; exit 2;; esac
if [ "$REPLICA" -ge 4 ]; then echo "Replica is outside this job array." >&2; exit 2; fi
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=4
export OPENMM_CPU_THREADS=4
export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=4
export MKL_NUM_THREADS=4
mkdir -p results
# A lock refuses accidental concurrent repeats and also records failed attempts.
if ! mkdir "results/replica-$REPLICA.lock"; then
  echo "Replica already attempted. Keep its results; use a fresh results directory for a new attempt." >&2
  exit 2
fi
# Verify immutable bundle files before running any scientific tests.
python -c "from chromatin_studio.batch import verify_bundle; verify_bundle('.')"
# Scientific checks run on the same allocated node and requested platform.
python -m chromatin_studio.validation --platform CUDA --precision mixed --output "results/validation-$REPLICA.json"
python -m chromatin_studio.batch --model model.json --job job.json --replica "$REPLICA" --output "results/replica-$REPLICA"
